source.title: Fermanagh Herald, 12 October 1946, p. 5 ("Elections in Co. Fermanagh: Cahir Healy wins Newtownbutler seat"); Belfast News-Letter, 5 October 1946, p. 3 ("County and rural council results")
source.publisher: Fermanagh Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Votes as printed in the Herald; 487-470=17, printed majority 17. The News-Letter reports the same 17-vote majority.

note: Triennial election of Fermanagh County Council. The only contest was Newtownbutler; the Fermanagh Herald of 28 September 1946 prints the unopposed return of George Elliott for Enniskillen urban and, under 'Changes of personnel', the new unopposed members for Enniskillen Rural, Maguiresbridge and Monea. The Belfast News-Letter of 20 September 1946 independently reports Elliott's unopposed return. The unchanged unopposed members are not individually printed in the Herald's 1946 report; they are the members returned in 1939, and the Herald records that there was no contest and no change in their divisions. Filled from the Impartial Reporter's lists of Unionist candidates (22 and 29 August 1946, p. 5), where the selected candidate is the member previously carried: Ballinamallard, Clonelly, Laragh, Lisbellaw, Lisnaskea and Florencecourt. Recorded for Nationalist-held divisions from the selection lists and first-meeting reports in the Fermanagh Herald: Derrylea, Crom, Rosslea and Doon. Recorded from reports of the new council's meetings during the term: Brookeborough and Lack. Healy, the Nationalist M.P., defeated the outgoing Unionist, J. W. H. Johnston, who had held the division for 21 years.
